title: Autosuggest Engine — Presets & Quick-Apply UI (brainstorm)
body:
Context and goal:

This doc captures an exploratory sketch and backlog-level thinking for an "autosuggest engine" inside Optimize that surfaces recommended presets (batching, cache & quantization) and lets product engineers preview, adjust, and quick-apply them to a model route. The focus is fast experimentation and low-friction adoption: one-click previews, simulated cost/latency delta, and an audit trail for applied changes (canary rollouts handled elsewhere).

Why this is different from past recs UX: we want an interface that behaves like an IDE suggestion panel (non-blocking, inline, quickly reversible) rather than a full-playbook modal. The engine should propose presets based on: workload signature, historical token distribution, recent regressions from evals, and infra constraints (e.g., dedicated capacity vs hosted).

High-level user flows (sketch):

1) Discovery (Optimize route main): user clicks "Optimize suggestions" pill next to a route. A slim slide-over appears from the right with top 3 ranked presets (small cards).

2) Inspect preset: click a card -> expands into an inspector with 3 tabs: Summary, Sample Impact, Timeline & Rollout. Summary lists the concrete changes (batching: dynamic batch size 32, max-latency 150ms; cache: prefix-KV enabled, TTL=1h, partial-match threshold 0.9; quant: int8-4bit-mixed, knob: enable per-layer fallback). Each change has a tappable microcopy linking to docs.

3) Sample Impact: run a quick simulated run (server-side lightweight simulation) that shows: expected median latency (ms), 95p latency, per-token cost delta (%), sample response diff (short token-level diff highlight), and quality risk score (0-5). The risk score is based on eval-set regressions and heuristics. Important: simulation must run in <8s and default to historical aggregated metrics if simulation times out.

4) Quick Apply: "Apply as Draft" (creates a draft config on the route) or "Apply Canary" (creates a canary rollout config, requires a selected canary percentage). Both actions produce an event in the route audit log and an optional GitHub-style diff for infra-as-code flows. A confirmation step shows a concise checklist of safety checks (model variant fallback, auto-rollback threshold).

Wireframe layout notes (visual):

- Slide-over width: 420px for main list. When inspector expands use 800–920px modal center stage.
- Cards: small tiles with top-left badge (Batch/Cash/Quant/mixed), one-line TL;DR, expected cost delta badge (+/-%), and a small confidence bar (3-line spark).
- Inspector header: preset name, estimated savings, quality risk pill (color-coded), last-run timestamp, owner (system or team name).

Microcopy suggestions (short):

- Suggestion card CTA: "Preview impact"
- Risk tooltip: "Quality risk is an estimate derived from test prompt regressions; always validate on a sample before commit."

Backlog bucket (epics & tickets):

- UX: Autosuggest slide-over + inspector (RED-1248) -> acceptance: list of presets, open inspector, ability to trigger simulation and see results.
- Runtime: lightweight sim endpoint (RED-1250) -> input: route, preset, sample-size=50; output: latency distribution, token-count delta, short diffs. Must have timeout and fallback path.
- Backend: Preset generator microservice (RED-1251) -> algorithmic rules + learned rules from workload clustering.
- Safety: Canary scaffolding + audit events (RED-1252).
- Analytics: instrumentation for suggestion open/show/apply conversion & per-preset CTR.

Acceptance criteria (alpha):

- User can open slide-over and see 3 suggestions within 1s for a route with recent traffic.
- Simulation returns results within 8s for typical routes or surface cached historical summary.
- Quick Apply creates a draft config and writes an audit event.

Open questions (we should resolve before eng grooming):

- What is the canonical source of truth for "workload signature"? (route traces vs storage). Need input from SRE on retention windows and privacy constraints.
- How is quantization recommended safely? Do we always pair quantize suggestions with an immediate fallback to higher-bit variant on quality regression?
- Are we comfortable showing per-token cost delta as a single number? Need product decision re: how to present uncertainty.
- Should the preview sim run on dedicated infra only or on hosted paths as well? Cost tradeoffs.

Prototype interactions (developer notes):

- Local mock: intercept Optimize API and return fake presets for demo. Keep cards data-driven: name, type, savings_pct, risk_score, details[].
- Sample diff view: token-diff with inline color highlights (green add, red remove). Allow toggling "masked" diffs for PII-sensitive prompts.

Edge cases / guardrails:

- For low-traffic routes (<100 req/day) only show conservative presets or "no suggestion" with advice to collect more traces.
- Explicitly show when suggestion relies on sparse data: "low confidence — insufficient traffic".

Metrics to track (initial):

- Suggestion CTR (open -> preview), Apply rate (preview -> apply), rollback rate within 24h, simulated vs live savings delta (accuracy of sim).

Phased rollout plan (product):

- Phase 0: internal-only alpha behind feature flag (optimize-team).
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for customers with Dedicated capacity.
- Phase 2: broad availability to hosted customers with rate limits for simulation calls.

Next steps / short TODOs (owners):

- [Ava] Draft slide-over wireframes in Figma and add example copy for each card (due: 2026-02-28).
- [Daniel] Prototype sim API stub and fake response shape for UX (due: 2026-03-07).
- [Priya] SRE check on retention windows & safe sampling (due: 2026-03-03).
- [Liam] Draft acceptance tests for canary apply flow incl. audit checks (due: 2026-03-10).

Notes-to-self / fragments (brainstorm shards):

- Consider a "Preset composer" where user can start from a recommended preset and toggle each knob (batch size slider, cache TTL, quant knob) and see delta update live. Could be heavy but valuable.
- UX candy: small inline explainer that shows a timeline of "what happens after apply" -> warm-up, cache priming, observed latency drift.
- Potential dark pattern to avoid: hiding potential quality regressions behind optimistic savings figures. Always show risk pill and link to sample differences.

References and inspiration:

- VSCode "quick fix" UX (non-blocking, small card suggestions).
- SRE runbooks that present "playbook step + impact".
- GitHub code suggestions (preview diff + apply).

If this looks reasonable we can convert to a 2-up Figma wireframe: small slide-over + expanded inspector. Put the UX tasks into the product sprint board and block prototype work until SRE thumbs-up on sampling plan.

End.
